public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 101

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/101](https://www.erdosproblems.com/101)
-/

@[expose] public section



namespace Erdos101

open EuclideanGeometry Filter Asymptotics

/--
The set of lines in $\mathbb{R}^2$ containing exactly $k$ points from a given set $S$.
-/
noncomputable def linesWithPointsFor (k : ℕ) (S : Set ℝ²) : Set (AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²) :=
  let determined_lines := { affineSpan ℝ {p, q} | (p ∈ S) (q ∈ S) (_ : p ≠ q) }
  { L ∈ determined_lines | (↑L ∩ S).ncard = k }

/--
The maximum number of lines containing exactly $4$ points among all sets $S$ of $n$
points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfying the condition that no five points are collinear.
-/
noncomputable def numLinesWithFourPointMax (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {((linesWithPointsFor 4 S).ncard)| (S : Set ℝ²)
    (_ : S.ncard = n) (_ : S.Finite) (_ : NonCollinearFor 5 S)}

/--
Given $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, no five of which are on a line, the number of
lines containing four points is $o(n^2)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_101 : (fun n => (numLinesWithFourPointMax n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n => (n : ℝ)^2) := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): formalize other results from the additional material

end Erdos101

reformulations.difference: The helper restricts to affine spans of distinct pairs of points of S, rather than ranging directly over all geometric lines. This matters for the unused parameters k = 0 and k = 1, but not for its only application here, k = 4.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every line containing four points of S contains two distinct such points and equals their affine span. Conversely, the span of two distinct points is a genuine line. Under the no-five-collinear hypothesis, containing four points means containing exactly four. The scratch lemma Review101.lines_iff_arbitrary_line proves the pair-witness restriction redundant for every k ≥ 2; Review101.nonCollinearFor_iff_line_bound proves the intended meaning of the no-five hypothesis for finite S.

reformulations.difference: The asymptotic bound is encoded using a natural-number supremum over configurations, a real cast, and IsLittleO. Erdős's 1987 formulation describes the maximum g(n) and asks whether g(n)/n² tends to zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For finite S, the counted lines form a subset of the image of S × S under the pair-span map. Thus their number is finite and at most |S|², and the supremum's set of values is bounded. Admissible configurations exist for every n, for example n distinct points on a parabola, so the natural supremum is the actual maximum. Scratch proofs establish equivalence to the uniform ε–N bound over all admissible S, and equivalence to convergence of the maximum divided by n² to zero. The denominator is nonzero eventually atTop.
